newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco El Teniente copper output hurt by snow.
newsitem.headline: Codelco El Teniente copper output hurt by snow.

text.p: Heavy weekend snowfall at Chilean state owned copper company Codelco's El Teniente mine has damaged equipment and the mine will need some two weeks to reach full production, said a division spokesman.
"We hope to be operating normally between now and two weeks time," the spokesman told Reuters.
The bad weather has cost the mine, Codelco's second largest division, most of its output since the blizzards struck Saturday, he said.
The bad weather damaged equipment at the mine's concentrator and only one of the pit's two railways is working, he said.

The concentrator, which shut down at the weekend, started working Tuesday but was not operating at full speed by Wednesday, he said. Meanwhile, the Caletones smelter was running below normal because of a shortage of concentrates and the mine has decided to bring forward scheduled maintenance by a week, he said.

"The smelter is only operating at half power because of the lack of concentrates so we've brought forward the maintenance of the El Teniente convertor which was due to start next week," said the official.
Violent weekend storms dumped two meters of snow at the mine which lies high in the Andes south of Santiago.
El Teniente, Codelco's largest underground pit, produced 345,000 tonnes of copper in 1996.
El Teniente has already lost 5,000 tonnes of copper -- almost all its output over the last five days, he said.
"We've already lost 5,000 tonnes of fine copper and there will be a few more tonnes (lost) in the next two weeks," he said.
The impact of the snow at the mine appeared more serious than officials had originally thought. They had said Tuesday that the pit was expected to be operating normally by the end of the day.
